The '''1959–60 European Cup''' was the fifth season of the [[UEFA Champions League|European Cup]], Europe's premier club [[association football|football]] tournament. The competition was won by [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], who beat [[Eintracht Frankfurt]] 7–3 in the [[1960 European Cup final|final]] at [[Hampden Park]], [[Glasgow]], on 18 May 1960,<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0219-0e8c04a491e7-267eb9e11c40-1000--madrid-win-a-fifth-consecutive-title/ |title=Madrid win a fifth consecutive title |website=[[UEFA]] |date=1 September 2014 |access-date=27 September 2024}}</ref> thanks to first ever hat-tricks scored in the final of the competition by [[Ferenc Puskás]] and [[Alfredo Di Stéfano]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://theanalyst.com/2024/05/champions-league-final-hat-trick |title=Who Has Scored a Champions League Final Hat-Trick? |website=TheAnalyst.com |first=David |last=Segar |publisher=Opta Analyst |date=23 May 2024 |access-date=27 September 2024}}</ref> It remains the [[European Cup and UEFA Champions League records and statistics|record score]] and record attendance for the European Cup final.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2020/may/18/real-madrid-eintracht-frankfurt-60-years-european-cup-hampden |title='We marked an era' – 60 years on from when Real won 7–3 at Hampden |work=The Guardian |date=18 May 2020 |access-date=27 September 2024 |first=Sid |last=Lowe}}</ref> It was Real Madrid's fifth consecutive title, which is a feat that no other club has matched.

It was also the first time that a German team, [[Eintracht Frankfurt]], reached the final. They were debutants in the competition and it wasn't until [[1983–84 European Cup]] and [[AS Roma]] that another debutants ended up on the losing side in the final.

The tournament saw the first participation by a Greek club, [[1958–59 Panhellenic Championship|Greek Champions]] [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiacos]], who had withdrawn from the [[1958–59 European Cup|previous season]] after being already placed in the bracket. It meant that no new country entered the competition for the first time since tournament inception.

==Teams==
A total of 27 teams were placed in the competition bracket, but finally only 26 participated since [[Kuopion Palloseura]] had withdrawn before playing first game.

Spain continued to be represented by two clubs, with Real Madrid qualifying as title holders and [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] as Spanish champions. [[PFC CSKA Sofia|CDNA Sofia]] appeared in the fourth edition of European Cup, with only Real Madrid having more appearances in the competition.

[[FK Inter Bratislava|Červená Hviezda Bratislava]], [[Boldklubben 1909]], Kuopion Palloseura, [[1. FC Frankfurt|Vorwärts Berlin]], Eintracht Frankfurt, [[Csepel SC|Csepel]], [[Sparta Rotterdam]], [[Linfield F.C.|Linfield]], [[ŁKS Łódź]], [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] and [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (football)|Fenerbahçe]] made their debut in the competition.

All entrants were their respective associations champions, except for Real Madrid and ŁKS Łódź, the latter being [[1958 Ekstraklasa|1958 champion]] and trailing by two points in spring of [[1959 Ekstraklasa|1959]].

The draw for the preliminary round took place in [[Cernobbio]], [[Province of Como|Como]], Italy, on 6 July 1959.<ref>''[[Corriere dello Sport]]'', 7 July 1959.</ref> As title holders, Real Madrid received a bye, and the remaining 26 teams were grouped geographically into two pots. The first two teams drawn in each pot also received byes, while the remaining clubs would play the preliminary round in August, September and October.
